# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫱 🫱 🫱 👌 🤏 🫱 🤏 👌 🤏 🫱 👌 🫱 🤏 👌 🫱 🫱 🤏 👌 🤏 👉 🫱 🤏 🫱 🫱 👌 🤏 👌 🤏 🫱 🤏 🤏 👌 🤏 🫱 🤏 🤏 👌 🫱 🫱 🫱 👌 🤏 🫱 🫱 🤏]

I see display 0, a purple light, and three wires in order: green, blue, yellow. Mute’s gesture message begins with Morse-coded “ORANGE”; I cannot yet interpret the remainder reliably. I will provide the bomb’s visible state to both hearing monkeys so Mute can select the relevant manual instruction and Blind has the shared state.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Visible bomb state: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT purple. WIRES: 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Your gestures begin Morse ORANGE; please send the applicable instruction after using this state.")
speak(to="blind", text="Visible bomb state: display zero, purple light, wires one green two blue three yellow. Mute is relaying manual information by gestures to me.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫱 🤏 🫱 🤏 👌 🫱 🫱 🤏 👌 🤏 🫱 🤏 👌 🤏 🫱 🫱 🤏 👌 🤏 🫱 🤏 🤏 👌 🤏 👉 🫱 🤏 🫱 🫱 👌 🤏 👌 🤏 🫱 🤏 🤏 👌 🤏 🫱 🤏 🤏 👌 🫱 🫱 🫱 👌 🤏 🫱 🫱 🤏]

The light has changed from purple to yellow while the display remains 0 and the wire order remains green, blue, yellow. Mute’s first gesture message decodes as “ORANGE YELLOW”; the new message does not yet form a clear English instruction under the same Morse convention. I will report the changed state and ask Mute to send an explicit action sentence; Blind should not cut or operate anything until then.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Update: light is now YELLOW; display remains 0; wires remain 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. Your prior Morse decoded ORANGE YELLOW. Please Morse an explicit instruction, e.g. CUT BLUE / PRESS / WAIT.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not cut or operate anything yet. Visible state now: display 0, yellow light, wires green-blue-yellow. Mute has not yet conveyed a clear actionable instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🫱 🫱 👌 🤏 🫱 👌 🤏 🤏 👌 🫱]

The gesture message decodes as “WAIT” (Morse: W A I T). The visible light is now orange; display remains 0 and the wires remain green, blue, yellow. Blind should wait and make no physical action.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's instruction decodes as WAIT. Do not cut, press, pull, or otherwise operate the bomb. Current visible state: display 0, orange light, wires green-blue-yellow.")
speak(to="mute", text="I decoded your latest Morse gesture as WAIT. Current visible state: display 0, orange light, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫱 🤏 🫱 🤏 👌 🤏 🤏 🫱 👌 🫱 👌 🤏 🫱 🫱 👌 🤏 👌 🫱 🤏 🫱 🤏 👌 🤏 👌 🤏 🫱 🤏 🤏 👌 🤏 🫱 🤏 🤏 👌 🫱 🫱 🫱 👌 🤏 🫱 🫱 🤏]

The light is purple again. Using the established Morse convention (🤏 = dot, 🫱 = dash, 👌 = letter break), Mute’s message decodes as “CUT WECELLOP,” which is not a valid wire instruction. I will ask for a resend with clear word breaks and tell Blind not to act on an ambiguous decoding.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your Morse decodes as CUT WECELLOP, which is not a recognizable action or wire colour. Please resend the exact instruction, with clear letter separators and a pause/word gap between words. Current state: display 0, purple light, wires green blue yellow.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not operate yet. Mute's latest relayed instruction decodes ambiguously as 'CUT WECELLOP,' not a valid wire colour. Current visible state: display 0, purple light, wires green-blue-yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🫱 🫱 👌 🤏 🫱 👌 🤏 🤏 👌 🫱]

Mute’s latest Morse message again decodes as “WAIT.” The light is yellow; display is still 0; wires remain green, blue, yellow. No physical action should be taken.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="WAIT. Mute's latest gesture message decodes clearly as WAIT. Do not operate the bomb. Visible state: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.")
speak(to="mute", text="Decoded WAIT. Current visible state: display 0, yellow light, wires green-blue-yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🫱 🫱 👌 🤏 🫱 👌 🤏 🤏 👌 🫱]

Mute again signals “WAIT.” The light is orange, with display 0 and wires green, blue, yellow unchanged. Blind should continue making no physical action.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="WAIT. Mute again signals WAIT. Do not touch, cut, press, or pull anything. Visible state: display 0, orange light, wires green-blue-yellow.")
speak(to="mute", text="Decoded WAIT. Visible state remains display 0, orange light, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🤏 🤏 🫱 🫱]

The latest Morse gesture decodes unambiguously as “3.” Mute previously conveyed “CUT” during the purple-light state, and now supplies the wire number. With the light purple, wire 3 is the yellow wire. I will tell Blind to cut wire 3, while reporting the state to Mute.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="CUT WIRE 3 NOW: the yellow wire. Mute's latest Morse is clearly number 3, following their earlier CUT instruction. Visible state is display 0, purple light, wires 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow.")
speak(to="mute", text="I decoded your latest gesture as 3. I have instructed Blind to cut wire 3, yellow, under the current purple light.")
```
